subject: Spanska 4
title: Conditional tense and si-clauses
sourceSummary: The conditional tense and hypothetical si-clauses with the imperfect subjunctive, as in "si tuviera tiempo, iría...".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Yo ___ (viajar) por el mundo si tuviera dinero."
questions.opener: The conditional is formed with the infinitive + the endings -ía, -ías, -ía...
questions.explanation: The conditional is formed with infinitive + -ía: "viajaría" (I would travel). This is the main clause's tense in a hypothetical si-clause about an unlikely/impossible present.

questions.prompt: Which structure is correct for a hypothetical si-clause about the present?
questions.opener: The si-clause (subordinate clause) takes the imperfect subjunctive, the main clause takes the conditional.
choices: Si tuviera tiempo, iría al gimnasio.
Si tengo tiempo, iría al gimnasio.
Si tuviera tiempo, voy al gimnasio.
Si tendría tiempo, iría al gimnasio.
questions.explanation: A hypothetical si-clause about the present: si + imperfect subjunctive (tuviera) in the subordinate clause, conditional (iría) in the main clause. The conditional may never follow "si" directly — that's a common mistake (compare option 4: "si tendría").

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Ellos ___ (poder) ayudarnos si supieran la verdad."
questions.opener: "Poder" has an irregular stem in the conditional: podr-.
questions.explanation: "Poder" has an irregular stem in the conditional: podr- + endings → "podrían" (they would be able to). The same irregular stem is used in the future tense.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Si yo ___ (ser) tú, no lo haría."
questions.opener: The imperfect subjunctive of "ser" has the stem fue- + the endings -ra/-ras/-ra...
questions.explanation: Imperfect subjunctive of "ser": fuera, fueras, fuera, fuéramos, fuerais, fueran. This form is used in si-clauses about a hypothetical present: "Si yo fuera tú..." (If I were you...).

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly describes something that did NOT happen in the past?
questions.opener: An impossible/contrary-to-fact past situation requires the pluperfect subjunctive + the conditional perfect.
choices: Si hubiera estudiado más, habría aprobado el examen.
Si estudiaba más, aprobaría el examen.
Si estudiara más, habría aprobado el examen.
Si hubiera estudiado más, aprobaría el examen.
questions.explanation: For contrary-to-fact past events: si + pluperfect subjunctive (hubiera estudiado) in the subordinate clause, conditional perfect (habría aprobado) in the main clause. The sentence means "If I had studied more, I would have passed the exam" — but didn't study, and didn't pass.

questions.prompt: Choose the most polite phrase: "¿___ decirme la hora, por favor?"
questions.opener: The conditional softens a request, similar to Swedish "skulle du kunna..." or English "could you...".
questions.explanation: The conditional ("podría", would be able to) makes a request more polite and softened. "Puede" (indicative, can) also works but sounds more direct. "Puedo" means "I can" and "pudo" is preterite — both wrong in this context.

questions.prompt: Correct the errors: "Si yo tendría más tiempo libre, aprendería tocar la guitarra."
questions.opener: A common mistake: the conditional cannot follow "si" directly in a hypothetical clause.
questions.answer: Si yo tuviera más tiempo libre, aprendería a tocar la guitarra.
steps: "Si tendría" is wrong — the clause after "si" in a hypothetical statement about the present must be in the imperfect subjunctive, not the conditional: "tuviera".
The main clause "aprendería" (conditional) is correct as it stands.
The preposition "a" is also missing between "aprender" and the infinitive: "aprender a tocar" is the correct construction in Spanish.
Full sentence: "Si yo tuviera más tiempo libre, aprendería a tocar la guitarra."

questions.prompt: How are the three types of si-clauses formed (real, hypothetical present, contrary-to-fact past)?
questions.opener: Three patterns to keep apart, plus the conditional's irregular stems.
questions.answer: 1) Real/likely (type 1): si + present indicative, main clause in present or future — "Si tengo tiempo, voy/iré". 2) Hypothetical/unlikely present (type 2): si + imperfect subjunctive, main clause in the conditional — "Si tuviera tiempo, iría". 3) Contrary-to-fact past (type 3): si + pluperfect subjunctive, main clause in the conditional perfect — "Si hubiera tenido tiempo, habría ido". Irregular conditional stems (same as the future tense): tener→tendr-, poder→podr-, hacer→har-, decir→dir-, salir→saldr-, querer→querr-, saber→sabr-, poner→pondr-, venir→vendr-.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Yo ___ (decir) la verdad si me preguntaran."
questions.opener: "Decir" has an irregular stem in the conditional: dir-.
questions.explanation: "Decir" has an irregular stem in the conditional: dir- + endings → "diría" (I would say).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Si ___ (hacer) buen tiempo mañana, iremos a la playa."
questions.opener: This is a real, likely si-clause (type 1) about the future, not a hypothetical one.
questions.explanation: A real/likely si-clause (type 1) takes the present indicative in the subordinate clause: "si hace buen tiempo", with the main clause in the future ("iremos").

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Nosotros ___ (hacer) un viaje si tuviéramos más dinero."
questions.opener: "Hacer" has an irregular stem in the conditional: har-.
questions.explanation: "Hacer" has an irregular stem in the conditional: har- + endings → "haríamos" (we would make/take).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Si hubieras llegado a tiempo, no ___ (perder) el tren."
questions.opener: A contrary-to-fact past (type 3) requires the conditional perfect in the main clause: habría + past participle.
questions.explanation: Contrary-to-fact past: si + pluperfect subjunctive (hubieras llegado) in the subordinate clause, conditional perfect (habrías perdido) in the main clause.

questions.prompt: Choose the most polite phrase: "¿___ tú acompañarme al médico?" (querer)
questions.opener: "Querer" has an irregular stem in the conditional: querr-.
questions.explanation: "Querer" has an irregular stem in the conditional: querr- + endings → "querrías" (would you want to), a polite question.

questions.prompt: Which si-clause describes a real, likely situation in the present/future?
questions.opener: Only one of these four options is type 1 (real/likely).
choices: Si tengo tiempo, iré al cine.
Si tuviera tiempo, iría al cine.
Si hubiera tenido tiempo, habría ido al cine.
Si tendría tiempo, iría al cine.
questions.explanation: "Si tengo tiempo, iré al cine" is a real/likely si-clause (type 1): present indicative + future. The others describe a hypothetical present, a contrary-to-fact past, or are grammatically incorrect (the conditional can never follow "si" directly).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Ella ___ (saber) la respuesta si hubiera estudiado más."
questions.opener: "Saber" has an irregular stem in the conditional: sabr-.
questions.explanation: "Saber" has an irregular stem in the conditional: sabr- + endings → "sabría" (she would know).
